instructions: The night before: melt 7 tbsp of the butter in a small pan over low heat. Take it off the heat and let it cool for about 10 minutes, until it's warm but no longer hot.
In a large bowl, whisk the 2 eggs with the 1/2 cup sugar, 1 tsp honey and 1 tsp vanilla by hand for about 1 minute, until the sugar is mixed in and the eggs look a little foamy.
In another bowl, whisk 3/4 cup of the flour with the 3/4 tsp baking powder. Add it to the eggs and stir with a spatula until no dry flour shows.
Pour in the cooled butter, finely grate in the zest of half the lemon and whisk gently until the batter is smooth and glossy.
Press plastic wrap right onto the surface of the batter and refrigerate it overnight, or up to 24 hours.
Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle.
Melt the last 1 tbsp butter and brush it into every cavity of a 12 cavity metal madeleine pan. Dust the pan with the last 1 tbsp flour, then turn it over and tap out the extra.
Spoon the cold batter into the cavities, filling each one almost to the top. Don't spread it out. It flattens in the oven.
Bake for 3 minutes. Then turn the oven off and leave the madeleines inside for 8 to 10 minutes. No peeking. This is when the bump on top forms.
Turn the oven back on to 325°F and bake for 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the tops spring back when you press one lightly.
Let them cool in the pan for 5 minutes. Then turn them out and stand them on their sides on a plate to finish cooling.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
advance_prep_notes: Make the batter the night before so it chills overnight.
method_notes: All three whisk eggs and sugar, fold in flour and melted butter that has cooled, flavor the batter with lemon zest and bake in a buttered tin until the edges are golden and the tops have a bump. Baking Like a Chef (from Alain Ducasse's cooking school) uses equal weights of egg, sugar, butter and flour with honey, vanilla and baking powder, chills the batter overnight or a full day, and starts the bake at 425°F before switching the oven off for the bump. RecipeTin Eats whips the eggs harder, adds milk and oil, chills the batter at least 6 hours and bakes at 390°F for 10 minutes; Not Quite Nigella makes a small batch with cake flour and no chilling step. This one follows Ducasse's ratios and bake, scaled to one 12 cavity pan.
